publication: Ambulance Quality Indicators — Ambulance Systems Indicators

ambulance-calls.label: Emergency calls
ambulance-calls.definition: Emergency calls recorded by the ambulance service.

ambulance-incidents.label: Ambulance incidents
ambulance-incidents.definition: Incidents created from ambulance-service contacts and referrals.

ambulance-hear-treat.label: Resolved remotely (Hear & Treat)
ambulance-hear-treat.definition: Incidents with no face-to-face ambulance response.

ambulance-response.label: Face-to-face ambulance response
ambulance-response.definition: Incidents with a face-to-face response. A56 is defined as A53 + A54 + A55.

ambulance-alternative.label: Treated or referred without conveyance (See & Treat)
ambulance-alternative.definition: Face-to-face incidents where no patient was transported.

ambulance-conveyed-ae.label: Conveyed to A&E by ambulance
ambulance-conveyed-ae.definition: Face-to-face incidents where one or more patients were transported to an emergency department.

ambulance-other-conveyance.label: Conveyed somewhere other than A&E
ambulance-other-conveyance.definition: Face-to-face incidents where patients were transported to a facility other than an emergency department.

notes: The figures are annual sums of the twelve monthly AmbSYS returns from April 2024 to March 2025.
Hear & Treat is shown as a percentage of incidents; face-to-face response is also shown as a percentage of incidents.
See & Treat, conveyance to A&E and conveyance elsewhere are shown as percentages of face-to-face responses so that they form a meaningful operational split.
Ambulance-service geographies are much larger than ICBs and do not align directly with ECDS provider geographies.
